title: Flat terms of the explicit finite-projective ring dual
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, with A-modules realized on the bottom-topology one-object ringed site [def-pc-perfect-rhom-base-change-map]. Let P be a cochain complex such that every evaluated term P^n is finite projective over A. Define D=Hom_A^\bullet(P,A[0]) using the shared Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex], with the ring sheaf in degree zero. Then D^n is a flat sheaf of modules [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] for every integer n. No boundedness is required.

source.place: Tag 0A6A, lemma-base-change-RHom, clause (1), finite-projective dual argument; projectivity of the dual also Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Dual/Lemmas.lean, Module.dual_projective (lines 145-147)

proof.text: Define D as the actual shared Hom complex Hom(P,A[0]), not as a chosen witness. In degree n its product factors are Hom(P^p,A[0]^(p+n)). All factors except p=-n are zero. Projection to p=-n is an isomorphism: the inverse has the identity component there and zero components elsewhere; the product universal property verifies both inverse identities. On the bottom-topology one-object site, evaluation is an equivalence with A-modules (all restriction maps are identities and every presheaf is a sheaf). Internal Hom evaluates to linear Hom, and the tensor evaluates to module tensor. Hence D^n evaluates to the module dual of P^(-n).

For a finite projective module M choose a split presentation M -> A^r -> M with composite the identity. Dualizing reverses the arrows and again gives a split presentation, because precomposition preserves composition and identities. Coordinate linear functionals identify the dual of A^r with A^r. Thus the dual of M is projective and therefore flat (Mathlib Module.dual_projective and Module.Flat.of_projective). Tensoring with it preserves finite limits and colimits. Transport this exactness along evaluation and the tensor comparison to obtain SheafOfModules.IsFlat for each D^n. This proves the assertion without boundedness of P.
